lines.en: Hey, Ana! **What about** a picnic in the park on Saturday?
lines.pt: Oi, Ana! Que tal um piquenique no parque no sábado?

lines.en: Sounds great, but the forecast says rain. **I’d rather** go to the new food market.
lines.pt: Parece ótimo, mas a previsão é de chuva. Eu prefiro ir à nova feira de comidas.

lines.en: Good point. **Could you** check the opening hours on your phone?
lines.pt: Boa observação. Você poderia ver o horário de funcionamento no seu celular?

lines.en: Sure. It opens at ten. Oh, and **my order hasn’t arrived** yet. I bought a jacket online.
lines.pt: Claro. Abre às dez. Ah, e meu pedido ainda não chegou. Comprei uma jaqueta online.

lines.en: Then **let’s** stop by the post office first. **Would it be possible to** pick it up there?
lines.pt: Então vamos passar primeiro no correio. Seria possível retirá-la lá?

lines.en: Maybe. I’ll call them, and **I’d like to change** the delivery address if not.
lines.pt: Talvez. Vou ligar para eles e gostaria de mudar o endereço de entrega, se não.

lines.en: **To sum up:** post office at nine, market at ten, and Maya joins us after her class.
lines.pt: Resumindo: correio às nove, feira às dez e a Maya se junta a nós depois da aula.

lines.en: Perfect. **I’ll take care of** the message for Maya.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Eu cuido da mensagem para a Maya.

pages.title: A2 Situations Review

situation.text: Two friends meet in a plaza to plan a Saturday. In one short conversation they plan, ask for help, solve a delivery problem and sum up the plan. You review the A2 situations by doing them again, in a new context.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can move between planning, polite requests, problems and summaries in one conversation, using the main A2 expressions without notes.
canDo: Plan together: What about…? / I’d rather…
Ask for help: Could you…? / Would it be possible to…?
Solve a problem: My order hasn’t arrived. / I’d like to change…
Close with a summary: To sum up…
success: I explain and solve a problem.
pages.think: Which A2 situation is easiest for you now? Which one still needs practice?

teach.goal: Abrir a revisão espaçada: o aluno revisita situações do A2 em um contexto novo, sem lista de regras.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga quais situações do A2 ele já domina e quais quer treinar.
Pergunte “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma situação do A2 (viagem, trabalho, entrega, apresentação) e explica por quê.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final da aula.
extra: What was the most useful A2 lesson for you?
Which expression do you use most?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, then link them to today’s situation.
intro.group: One question per student, then ask a classmate the same question back.

pages.recall: Spaced review: planning (What about…?), work requests (Could you…?), deliveries (My order hasn’t arrived) and talks (To sum up…).

qs.q: What are you doing this weekend?
qs.pt: O que você vai fazer neste fim de semana?

qs.q: Who did you ask for help last week? What did you say?
qs.pt: A quem você pediu ajuda na semana passada? O que disse?

qs.q: Tell me about something that went wrong recently.
qs.pt: Conte algo que deu errado recentemente.

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier A2 content. Aim for longer answers: two or three connected sentences.

teach.goal: Retomar várias situações do A2 e identificar o que precisa de reforço.
extra: What was the last problem you solved in English?
Which situation is hardest for you?
support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Spaced review of the A2 patterns
pages.intro: Real conversations mix functions: you suggest, ask, explain a problem and sum up, often in one minute. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Friends suggest ideas, check the weather and the time, and choose a plan together.
A quick “Could you check…?” keeps the plan moving.
In many places, people check the forecast and have a backup plan for outdoor events.

qs.q: What do friends do when the weather is bad?
qs.pt: O que amigos fazem quando o tempo está ruim?

levels.A2: They change the plan: “I’d rather go to the market.”
levels.B1: They suggest an indoor plan, like a market or a café, and decide together.
levels.B2: They adapt quickly, proposing an alternative that fits the weather and everyone’s preferences.

qs.q: How do you ask a friend to check something for you?
qs.pt: Como pedir a um amigo para verificar algo?

levels.A2: Could you check the opening hours?
levels.B1: Could you check the opening hours on your phone while I look at the map?
levels.B2: Would you mind checking the opening hours? That would help us decide.

qs.q: Why is a short summary useful?
qs.pt: Por que um resumo curto é útil?

levels.A2: To check that everyone has the same plan.
levels.B1: A summary confirms who does what and when.
levels.B2: Summarizing the decisions prevents misunderstandings and confirms the next steps.

pages.compare: In Brazil, plans with friends often change at the last minute and are confirmed by message. In English, the phrase “To sum up” also works in a message: “So: post office at nine, market at ten.” How do you confirm plans?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural da revisão: como as funções do A2 se combinam numa conversa real.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com a forma como confirma planos com amigos.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q3: para confirmar quem faz o quê e quando.
extra: Do you check the weather before you plan?
How do you confirm a plan by message?
support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: resuma um plano de três pessoas em duas frases.

pass1.pt: O que os amigos estão fazendo?

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois 5 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: primeira ideia, problema, horário da feira, encomenda e primeira parada.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam as respostas antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 2: picnic · rain · ten · jacket · post office.
extra: Who changes the plan? Why?
Who will contact Maya?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: Why does Ana prefer the market?
What does Tom ask Ana to check?

opts: Post office at nine, market at ten
Market at nine, picnic at ten

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks de várias situações e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê o papel da Ana; você lê o do Tom.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: The forecast says rain · the opening hours · her order hasn’t arrived · post office at nine, market at ten
extra: Which part is planning? Which part is a request? Which part is a problem?
What would YOU suggest?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

errors.w: I rather go to the market.
errors.r: I’d rather go to the market.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Make a suggestion that includes both of you.

items.en: What about a picnic on Saturday?
I’d rather go to the market.
Could you check the opening hours?
To sum up: post office at nine.

pages.note: This is a spaced review: choose the five ★ expressions that you want to use without notes at the end of the class.

teach.goal: Revisão espaçada: reconhecer a função de cada chunk e escolher 5 para usar sem consulta.
solo: Pergunte “Which lesson did this come from?” antes de dar o significado.
Peça um exemplo próprio para cada ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão mais difícil e explica quando usa.
Compare em duplas: qual expressão vocês esquecem mais?
answers: Suggesting and preferring · Asking for help · Explaining a problem · Summing up
extra: Which expression do you forget most often?
support: Trabalhe só 3 das expressões ★ na primeira rodada.

patterns.name: Suggest and prefer
ex: I’d rather go to the market.

patterns.name: Ask politely
patterns.formula: **Could you** + base verb? · **Would it be possible to** + base verb?
ex: Could you check the opening hours?
Would it be possible to pick it up there?

patterns.name: Explain a problem
patterns.formula: **My order hasn’t arrived** / **I’d like to change** + noun
ex: I’d like to change the address.

patterns.name: Sum up
ex: To sum up, post office at nine.
To sum up, we meet at ten.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Would you like to have a picnic?
Could you please confirm the opening hours?
I am writing about a missing order.
To sum up, nine and ten.
In summary, we will meet at nine and ten.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules.

teach.goal: Revisar os padrões principais do A2 (sugerir/preferir e pedir com educação); os outros são expansão.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrão 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Change one word and say the new sentence.
Which pattern from earlier lessons do you want to review?
support: Fique só com What about… e Could you… na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combinar as três funções em uma fala de 3 frases.

errors.w: To sum up: we goes at ten.
errors.r: To sum up, we go at ten.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In fast speech, “could you” sounds like “couldja” and “would you” like “wouldja”. This is natural in casual American English. The goal is to be clear and natural, not to remove your accent.

own.prompt: Write one “Could you…?” and one “Would you like…?” question that you could really ask a friend.
own.criteria: Say them twice: slowly, then with “couldja / wouldja”. Did they sound smooth?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: redução (could you → couldja, would you → wouldja).
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e redução → usar em pergunta própria.
Modele devagar e normal; mostre que as palavras se unem.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma pergunta própria com a redução.
answers: Identify 1: Could you call them? · Identify 2: Would you like some coffee?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. It might rain on Saturday. You prefer a different plan.
opts: I’d rather go to the market.

items.q: 2. You need a friend to check the opening hours.
opts: Could you check the opening hours?

items.q: 3. Your jacket from an online store is late.
4. You want to close the plan.
opts: To sum up, post office at nine and market at ten.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: Would it be possible ___ pick it up today?
items.why: Would it be possible + to + verb.

ans: Could you check the hours, please?
Would it be possible to check the hours?
items.model: Could you check the hours, please?
items.why: Could you + verb turns a command into a polite request.

ans: I’d like to change the address.
I’d like to change the address, please.
items.model: I’d like to change the address.

items.npc: Should we meet at nine or ten?
opts: I’d rather meet at ten, if that’s okay.
items.why: Answer the choice and show a preference politely.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: revisar funções de várias aulas antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta e diga de qual aula é o padrão.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: I’d rather go to the market. · 2: Could you check the opening hours? · 3: My order hasn’t arrived yet. · 4: To sum up, …
Gap: What · to · Could you check the hours, please? · I’d like to change the address. · I’d rather meet at ten.
extra: Say each correct answer aloud with “couldja” where natural.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

errors.r: Would it be possible to send?

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — a full Saturday

brief.teacher: You are the friend (add a problem each time!).
brief.student: You plan a Saturday with a friend: suggest, ask for help, handle a problem and sum up.

orders: A picnic that might turn into a museum day
A lunch plan and a late online order
A trip to a market with a friend who arrives late
complications: Your order is late and you need to change the address.
Your friend can’t come at the agreed time.
The place is closed on Saturdays.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com o sábado real do aluno.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if two problems happen at once?
support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça que resolva dois problemas na mesma conversa e faça o resumo no fim.

errors.r: I can’t go because of the rain. / because it’s raining.

rounds.title: Suggest and prefer
rounds.task: Suggest a weekend plan. Your partner prefers something else.

rounds.title: Ask for help
rounds.task: Ask your partner to check or do something for the plan.
rounds.hint: Could you…? / Would it be possible to…?

rounds.title: Solve a problem
rounds.task: Something goes wrong: late order, rain or a closed place.
rounds.hint: My order hasn’t arrived. / I’d like to change…

rounds.title: Sum up
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair summarizes their final plan.

infogap.title: Saturday plan
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: You know the places
a.task: You know the places. Ask about the times.

b.title: You know the times
b.task: You know the times. Ask about the places.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição de funções diferentes com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 sugestão, ≥1 pedido e ≥1 resumo.
answers: Info gap: A tem os locais (Main Street, Plaza Square); B tem os horários (9:00, 10:00). Cada um completa perguntando.
extra: Where is the post office?
What time does the market open?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

errors.r: What time does the market open?

errors.w: It is in Plaza Square place.

pages.title: Group mission — a busy Saturday
pages.goal: Each group must plan a Saturday in English, deal with a problem and summarize the final plan.

missions.mission: Plan a day out. The weather is bad, so change the plan, and ask a friend to check a place’s hours.
A package is late and you have to be home on Saturday. Solve it by changing the delivery or the plan.
missions.constraint: Use “My order hasn’t arrived” and “I’d like to change…”.
missions.start: I have a problem: my order hasn’t arrived…

missions.mission: Organize a small dinner for four. Each person takes a task and promises to do it.
missions.constraint: Use “Would it be possible to…?” and “I’ll take care of…”; finish with “To sum up…”.
missions.start: Let’s plan the dinner. Could you…

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: combinar várias situações do A2 numa só conversa.
group: Cada grupo recebe papéis, restrição e missão. Alterne quem propõe e quem reage.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “What about the park?” → “I’d rather go to a café, it’s going to rain.” → “Could you check if it’s open?” → “To sum up: café at ten.”
extra: What if a friend wants a different plan?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend that plans a Saturday: suggest a plan, ask for help, mention a problem and sum up.
pages.model: Hi Tom! **What about** the food market on Saturday? **Could you** check when it opens? Also, **my order hasn’t arrived** yet, so **I’d like to change** the address. **To sum up:** post office at nine, market at ten. See you there!
checklist: I mentioned a problem and a solution.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta que reúne as funções revisadas.
solo: Peça a mensagem; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more request to your message.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

errors.w: To sum up: we meet at ten o’clock hours.
errors.r: To sum up, we meet at ten.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You changed topic and function easily (planning → request → problem).
prompts.improve: Example: Link “could you” as “couldja” in fast speech.
prompts.next: Example: Do the whole conversation without notes and keep it for two minutes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais. Observe o controle de várias funções na mesma conversa.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

items: Record a 60-second audio planning a day, asking for help and summing up.
Write a short message with a suggestion, a request, a problem and a summary.

Listen to the dialogue again and count how many functions you hear.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: sugerir/preferir, pedir com educação e resumir.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: What about a picnic? … I’d rather go to the market… · Could you check the opening hours? · To sum up, post office at nine and market at ten.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na missão final da unidade (próxima aula).

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Say it with short phrases and models.

ladder.say: What about the park? I’d rather go to the market. Could you check when it opens?
Since it might rain, I think we should go to the market instead, and I’ll check the hours myself.
ladder.goal: Explain and compare options with connectors.

ladder.say: Given the forecast, I’d suggest moving indoors; would you mind checking whether the market is open?
ladder.goal: Negotiate with nuance and appropriate register.

ladder.say: Weather permitting, the park would be lovely, but I wouldn’t want to risk it; shall we settle on the market?
The market seems the more prudent choice, so let’s commit to it and leave the park for a drier day.
ladder.goal: Manage the situation with precision and tact.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão e retomar as situações do A2.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
